name: Chapter 7: Structural Organisation in Animals
description: Tissues, organs and organ systems, and the morphology and anatomy of the frog

cards.term: What is a tissue?
cards.definition: A group of similar cells with intercellular substances performing a specific function

cards.term: How many basic tissue types make up all complex animals? Name them.
cards.definition: Four: epithelial, connective, muscular, neural

cards.term: What is an organ system?
cards.definition: Two or more organs performing a common function by physical and/or chemical interaction, e.g. digestive system

cards.term: Which organ does NCERT give as containing all four tissue types?
cards.definition: The heart

cards.term: Morphology vs anatomy, in animals?
cards.definition: Morphology: external appearance of organs and body parts. Anatomy: morphology of internal organs.

cards.term: What are epithelia?
cards.definition: Sheet-like tissues lining body surfaces, cavities, ducts and tubes, with one free surface

cards.term: To which class and phylum do frogs belong?
cards.definition: Class Amphibia, phylum Chordata

cards.term: Most common Indian frog (NCERT)?
cards.definition: Rana tigrina, the Indian bullfrog

cards.term: What is the current scientific name of the Indian bullfrog? (beyond NCERT)
cards.definition: Hoplobatrachus tigerinus: NCERT still uses the older name Rana tigrina; write NCERT's name in board exams

cards.term: Why are frogs called poikilotherms (cold-blooded)?
cards.definition: Their body temperature varies with the environment

cards.term: What are aestivation and hibernation in frogs?
cards.definition: Aestivation: summer sleep. Hibernation: winter sleep. Both in deep burrows.

cards.term: What does NCERT call the frog's protective colour change?
cards.definition: Mimicry (NCERT's term; the colour change is to hide from enemies, camouflage)

cards.term: Is the frog's colour change really mimicry? (correction)
cards.definition: Strictly, no. Blending with the background is camouflage (cryptic colouration). Mimicry means resembling another species. For NCERT-based MCQs, NCERT's word is "mimicry".

cards.term: Why is frog skin smooth and slippery?
cards.definition: Presence of mucus

cards.term: Dorsal and ventral colour of a frog?
cards.definition: Dorsal: olive green with dark irregular spots. Ventral: uniformly pale yellow.

cards.term: How does a frog take in water?
cards.definition: It never drinks; it absorbs water through the skin

cards.term: Into what is a frog's body divided? What is absent?
cards.definition: Head and trunk; neck and tail absent

cards.term: What protects the frog's eyes in water?
cards.definition: A nictitating membrane

cards.term: What receives sound in a frog?
cards.definition: A membranous tympanum on either side of the eyes

cards.term: Digits on fore and hind limbs?
cards.definition: Fore limb: four. Hind limb: five (larger, muscular, webbed for swimming).

cards.term: How can a male frog be told from a female?
cards.definition: Males have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limb

cards.term: Figure 7.1 · External features of frog
Why is the frog's alimentary canal short?
cards.definition: Frogs are carnivores, so the intestine is reduced

cards.text: Path of food: mouth → {{c1::buccal cavity}} → {{c2::pharynx}} → oesophagus → {{c3::stomach}} → intestine → rectum → {{c4::cloaca}}.

cards.term: How does a frog capture food?
cards.definition: With its bilobed tongue

cards.term: What is chyme?
cards.definition: Partially digested food passed from the stomach to the duodenum

cards.term: What reaches the duodenum through the common bile duct?
cards.definition: Bile (from the gall bladder) and pancreatic juice

cards.term: What do bile and pancreatic juice do?
cards.definition: Bile emulsifies fat; pancreatic juice digests carbohydrates and proteins

cards.term: Where is digested food absorbed?
cards.definition: By villi and microvilli on the inner wall of the intestine

cards.term: Figure 7.2 · Internal organs of frog (digestive system)
What is cutaneous respiration? When?
cards.definition: Gas exchange through the skin by diffusion: in water, and during aestivation and hibernation

cards.term: Which organs does a frog breathe with on land?
cards.definition: Buccal cavity, skin and lungs

cards.term: What is pulmonary respiration?
cards.definition: Respiration by the lungs

cards.term: Describe frog lungs.
cards.definition: A pair of elongated, pink, sac-like structures in the upper trunk (thorax)

cards.term: What type of vascular system does a frog have?
cards.definition: Well developed, closed, plus a lymphatic system

cards.term: Chambers of the frog heart? What covers it?
cards.definition: Three: two atria, one ventricle; covered by the pericardium

cards.term: What is the sinus venosus?
cards.definition: A triangular structure joining the right atrium; it receives blood through the vena cava

cards.term: Into what does the frog ventricle open?
cards.definition: A sac-like conus arteriosus on the ventral side

cards.term: Hepatic portal vs renal portal system?
cards.definition: Hepatic portal: between liver and intestine. Renal portal: between kidney and lower parts of the body.

cards.term: Frog RBCs: nucleated or not?
cards.definition: Nucleated, with haemoglobin

cards.term: How does lymph differ from blood?
cards.definition: It lacks RBCs and a few proteins

cards.term: Single or double circulation in frog?
cards.definition: Single circulation (NCERT summary): the 3-chambered heart mixes some blood. Many texts call it "incomplete double" circulation.

cards.term: Name the frog's excretory organs.
cards.definition: A pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca, urinary bladder

cards.term: Describe frog kidneys.
cards.definition: Compact, dark red, bean-like, on both sides of the vertebral column

cards.term: What are the units of the frog kidney?
cards.definition: Uriniferous tubules (nephrons)

cards.term: Ureters in male vs female frogs?
cards.definition: Male: ureters act as urinogenital ducts into the cloaca. Female: ureters and oviducts open separately.

cards.term: What nitrogenous waste does a frog excrete?
cards.definition: Urea: it is ureotelic

cards.term: Name the endocrine glands of the frog.
cards.definition: Pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals, gonads

cards.term: Three divisions of the frog nervous system?
cards.definition: Central (brain, spinal cord), peripheral (cranial, spinal nerves), autonomic (sympathetic, parasympathetic)

cards.term: How many pairs of cranial nerves in a frog?
cards.definition: Ten

cards.term: What encloses the frog brain?
cards.definition: A bony brain box, the cranium

cards.text: Frog brain: forebrain has {{c1::olfactory lobes}}, paired {{c2::cerebral hemispheres}} and unpaired {{c3::diencephalon}}; midbrain has a pair of {{c4::optic lobes}}; hindbrain has {{c5::cerebellum}} and {{c6::medulla oblongata}}.

cards.term: Through what does the medulla oblongata pass out?
cards.definition: The foramen magnum, continuing into the spinal cord

cards.term: Frog sense organs
cards.definition: Touch: Sensory papillae; Taste: Taste buds; Smell: Nasal epithelium; Vision: Eyes; Hearing: Tympanum with internal ears

cards.term: Which frog sense organs are well organised structures?
cards.definition: Eyes and internal ears; the rest are cell clusters around nerve endings

cards.term: What kind of eyes does a frog have?
cards.definition: Simple eyes (one unit each), in the orbits

cards.term: Besides hearing, what does the frog ear do?
cards.definition: Balancing (equilibrium)

cards.term: Describe frog testes and their attachment.
cards.definition: A pair of yellowish ovoid testes attached to the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum, the mesorchium

cards.term: How many vasa efferentia arise from frog testes, and where do they go?
cards.definition: 10–12; they enter the kidneys and open into Bidder's canal

cards.term: What passes out through the cloaca?
cards.definition: Faecal matter, urine, and sperms

cards.term: Figure 7.3 · Male reproductive system of frog
Is there a functional connection between frog ovaries and kidneys?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: How many ova can a mature female frog lay at a time?
cards.definition: 2500–3000

cards.term: Fertilisation and development in frogs?
cards.definition: Fertilisation external, in water; a larval tadpole undergoes metamorphosis

cards.term: Figure 7.4 · Female reproductive system of frog
How are frogs useful to us?
cards.definition: They eat insects and protect crops; they are a link in food chains and webs
